title: Wanting to understand how Louis Armstrong played
summary: After hearing Armstrong, Keppard and Shoffner he never meant to be another Louis but studied his cliches.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Uh-huh. What would you say was the -- back then, in your early days in the '20's. What were the great events in your life?
In your career, what did you want to be in those days? Did you want to be another Louis Armstrong, or did you --
Well, after hearing Louis Armstrong, and Freddie Keppard Gebhardt, and then I heard -- I was impressed also by a fellow named Bob Shafner Staffner --
Who replaced Louis with King Oliver,
right? I knew I would never be another Louis Armstrong, I had no even thought about that.

But I wanted to be able to play like him. I wanted to be able to understand how he played and why he played certain things at different times. In fact I was on his tail all the time, studying little cliches that he would do. Course, naturally, a lot of them he learned from King Oliver. Course, I also listened to King Oliver a long time.
